sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.05% (-19 bp in a month), 2-year 4.67% (-25 bp); 2s10s curve +38 bp (+6 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 3.98% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.96 (+0.6% in a month, +3.7% YTD). USD/BRL 5.385 (+3.1% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.650 (-0.9%); USD/MXN 18.79 (+4.5%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 +0.7% in a month (+12.9% YTD); VIX 16.4. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 100.19 $/bbl (+14.8% in a month), Brent 109.49, ULSD 4.514 $/gal (+4.2%), natural gas 2.93 (-12.1%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -0.3% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.7%, Hang Seng -6.4%, yuan +0.9% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

us_econ: Inflation: CPI 3.7% y/y (2026-09), core 2.6%; core 3-month annualized 3.4%; core PCE 3.0%. Jobs: payrolls +29k in 2026-09 (3-month average +51k), unemployment 4.2% (+0.1), wages 3.0% y/y. Growth: real GDP 2.2% annualized in 2026-Q2, consumer spending 3.8%. Policy: fed funds target 3.75-4.0% (effective 3.88%); 2-year Treasury 4.67% (+0.79 vs fed funds: market pricing hikes); 10-year breakeven inflation 2.38%, real 10-year 2.67%. Farm prices (PPI farm products) +1.5% y/y; food-at-home CPI +1.8% y/y. For ags: high real yields and a firm dollar weigh on fund demand for commodities; sticky inflation keeps rates high (carry and storage costs up); a weak job market or falling real incomes hits meat and dairy demand first.

energy.read: Gas storage 3,644 Bcf (week to 2026-10-16), +77 Bcf vs a 5-year average +76 for the week; -1 Bcf (-0.0%) vs the 5-year average, -154 vs last year. Crude stocks 410.6 mb (-1.9 mb on the week, -3.8% vs 5-yr avg); gasoline +3.9 mb, distillate -1.5 mb; refinery utilization 92.8%. 3-2-1 crack $48.44/bbl (ULSD $90.07, gasoline $27.63). Options: NG IV 70% vs RV 50%; CL IV 51% vs RV 39%; HO IV 63% vs RV 45%; RB IV 50% vs RV 29%. For ags: diesel and natural gas set farm fuel, drying and nitrogen fertilizer costs; crude and gasoline drive ethanol and biodiesel margins (corn, soybean oil).
